name: Argon2
listed_description: The password hash Argon2, winner of PHC. (awesome-cpp Cryptography)
reason: No numeric comparison against any named baseline. The README 'Benchmarks' section (make bench) prints only Argon2d/Argon2i absolute cycles per byte and seconds for 1 MiB to 4096 MiB (for example 4096 MiB, 2 threads: 2.15 cpb, 13.0 s); CHANGELOG.md has no speed figures. The checked-in specification (argon2-specs.pdf, read via raw.githubusercontent.com) gives Table 4 (Argon2d 1.3 cpb at 1 thread, 0.6 cpb at 4 threads on an i7-4500U, gcc 4.8.2 -O3 -mavx) and says Argon2 'equals in performance with the PHC finalists' and Argon2d is about three times as fast as Argon2i, but it names scrypt, bcrypt, PBKDF2, Catena and Lyra2 only qualitatively and compares no timings. Directional claims only.

name: Bcrypt
listed_description: A cross platform file encryption utility. Encrypted files are portable across all supported operating systems and processors. (awesome-cpp Cryptography)
reason: The project page (Blowfish-based file encryption utility, BSD licence, last news September 11, 2002) offers one performance statement, '1.1 is immensely faster than 1.0', plus roughly 50% (compression off) and 66% (compression on) of the memory of 1.0, all self versus its own earlier release, with no timings, no hardware and no other tool as baseline. No benchmark or comparison against another encryption tool reachable.

name: crypto-algorithms
listed_description: Basic implementations of standard cryptography algorithms (AES, SHA, etc.) in C. (awesome-cpp Cryptography)
reason: The README says outright 'These algorithms are not optimized for speed or space' and are meant for readability and educational use (and 'not cryptographically secure implementations'). No benchmark, timing or comparison against any library in the repository, and none found in a shootout.

name: digestpp
listed_description: C++11 header-only message digest (hash) library. (awesome-cpp Cryptography)
reason: No numbers anywhere reachable. The README has no benchmark section and its Known limitations say the bundled providers are plain C++ and 'may be slower than SIMD optimized implementations'; the repository (algorithm, cmake, detail, docs, test directories) holds no benchmark or speed test, only functional tests and test vectors. It is a wrapper-style API layer ('Derived from cppcrypto'), and no comparison against OpenSSL, Crypto++ or Botan is given.
